name: Eco-Capitalism
summary: Eco-capitalism holds that capitalism can solve environmental problems if nature is counted as capital and pollution as a market failure. Its signature tools are carbon taxes, tradable emission permits and secure property rights, plus technological and resource-productivity gains that let firms profit from cutting waste. It is the market-oriented counterpart to eco-socialism and accepts more regulation than laissez-faire capitalism, but not planning or public ownership.
scope: The mainstream strand documented as eco-capitalism, environmental capitalism or green capitalism: Hawken, Lovins and Lovins' Natural Capitalism (1999) for the business and resource-productivity case, carbon-pricing economics, and Anderson and Leal's free-market environmentalism (PERC) for the property-rights case. It excludes eco-socialist, degrowth and eco-authoritarian strands; most social, cultural and foreign-policy questions are low-confidence inferences because these sources never address them.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Eco-capitalism holds markets can protect the environment once externalities are priced, but concedes they fail without such rules, so agreement is qualified.

public-ownership.rationale: Free-market environmentalists prefer property rights and markets over political control, and see public commons as prone to rent-seeking; some energy regulation is accepted.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Natural Capitalism talks of cutting income taxes and shifting the burden to pollution and resource use, not of raising taxes on the rich.

unions-good.rationale: Natural Capitalism mentions union cooperation in just transitions for workers, but the market-environmentalist literature is silent.

property-fundamental.rationale: Free-market environmentalism makes clearly defined, protected property rights central, though adherents accept pollution limits override them.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The article says eco-capitalism involves more regulation than unregulated capitalism, with emission limits that force firms to cut pollution.

worker-ownership.rationale: Natural Capitalism keeps conventional firms and markets, and nothing in it calls for collective worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The ideology has no position on surveillance and market-minded adherents are split between security and liberty views.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No stated position; free-market adherents lean libertarian but business-minded greens are mixed.

state-harmful.rationale: Eco-capitalists assign the state an essential role in setting caps, taxes and market rules, so they reject the claim that it is unnecessary.

decide-locally.rationale: PERC favours local, voluntary conservation, yet carbon pricing and Kyoto-style trading need national or international rules.

traditional-family.rationale: Nothing in the ideology backs traditional-family doctrine; business-oriented greens tend toward social moderation.

more-religion-public.rationale: The ideology is secular and technocratic and gives religion no political role.

gender-social-construct.rationale: No position in the sources; adherents are divided.

gradual-change.rationale: The approach works through incremental price signals and policy within existing markets, and its critics note it keeps the system intact.

free-trade.rationale: Markets are the preferred mechanism and international emissions trading is central, so free trade is supported, with environmental conditions.

nation-first.rationale: Climate externalities are global and solved through Kyoto-style international markets, so putting national interest ahead of cooperation sits badly.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: No position in the literature; adherents are mixed.

open-borders.rationale: Not an eco-capitalist aim; market liberals may accept free movement, but it is not part of the ideology.

limit-growth.rationale: Eco-capitalists hold that environmental benefit and profit can coincide, so growth need not be limited, though they favour measuring it better, for instance with the Genuine Progress Indicator.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Carbon pricing is meant as a strong response, but adherents favour price-based tools over drastic command measures.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Natural Capitalism rests on resource productivity and biomimicry, and Hawken and others expect cheap solar and efficiency to drive change; the claim of 'most problems' is strong, hence 1.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Natural Capitalism's excerpt lists nuclear among sources to be phased out, but market adherents often accept it on carbon grounds.

revolution-justified.rationale: The ideology seeks reform through market instruments and is the right-wing counterpart to eco-socialism, rejecting revolutionary overthrow.

experts-over-public.rationale: Economists' consensus underpins carbon pricing, but nothing says experts should override voters.

central-planning.rationale: Eco-capitalism relies on prices and tradable permits rather than planning, and holds markets can be environmentally beneficial.

socialized-markets.rationale: Natural Capitalism keeps ordinary firms in market-based systems; worker or public ownership is not its condition for markets.

land-value-tax.rationale: Some free-market environmentalists favour land value taxation, but it is not a core eco-capitalist position.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Eco-capitalist proposals shift taxes toward pollution and resources and away from incomes; heavy inheritance taxes are not part of them.

basic-income.rationale: Pigouvian revenue can fund a dividend according to some free-market thinkers, but it is not a general eco-capitalist position.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Eco-capitalists want prices and incentives to steer investment, though governments subsidise renewables and set standards, so opposition is only mild.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Eco-capitalism operates entirely within money, wage and market relations.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting wages and prices contradict the market-price mechanism eco-capitalists rely on.

one-party-rule.rationale: Eco-capitalism works through market and democratic institutions; one-party rule is the model of eco-authoritarianism, which it opposes.

workers-councils.rationale: Eco-capitalism is the right-wing counterpart of eco-socialism and does not seek council power.

natural-rulers.rationale: The literature appeals to democratic systems and equal market participation, not natural ability to rule.

war-builds-character.rationale: Eco-capitalism focuses on prosperity through peaceful markets and has no glorification of war.

separate-church-state.rationale: A secular market-based approach assumes it, though sources are silent.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: A secular, technocratic market ideology; its policy basis is economics and natural-capital accounting, not scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Free-market environmentalists rely on common-law tort courts as public institutions; private provision of policing and defence is not part of it.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Nothing in a market-global ideology supports ethnic homogeneity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Eco-capitalism sees market incentives and innovation, not class conflict, as the mover of change; Marxist-influenced critics make the class argument.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Market-based approaches stress incentives and opportunity, and income equality is a concern only of critics' indicators such as the GPI.

civilizational-union.rationale: Eco-capitalism looks to global markets and treaties such as Kyoto, not religious or civilisational blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The approach works by harnessing self-interest through prices and profit, e.g. firms that profit from cutting pollution, though it does not make self-interest a moral doctrine.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Property-rights and tort-based approach stresses individual rights over communal duty.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Nature is treated as natural capital whose value rests on services to human wealth, in contrast to deep ecology.

limit-population.rationale: Hardin is cited as an early market voice on overpopulation, but most adherents do not make population control a plank.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Natural Capitalism argues industry can be remade through productivity and biomimicry, an 'Industrial Revolution', not a disaster to reverse.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Eco-capitalists want fast adoption of efficient and renewable technology, though not at the cost of disrupting institutions.

human-enhancement.rationale: Unrelated to the environmental market literature.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Nothing in the sources supports delegating government decisions to AI.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Privacy and security are outside environmental-market thinking, and market-minded adherents divide between civil-liberties and law-enforcement views.

restore-past-order.rationale: The ideology is forward-looking and modernising, aiming at a new industrial revolution.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Natural Capitalism stresses that firms profit from efficiency and that pragmatic results justify change; this is a pragmatic stance.

direct-action.rationale: Change is sought through price signals, markets and legislation, not direct action.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Eco-capitalism embraces modern production and technology, aiming to improve rather than abandon industry.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Specialised market production is assumed throughout.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution is through markets, prices and wages.

production-for-use.rationale: Profit is the engine that eco-capitalism aims to align with environmental protection.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Profit is seen as legitimate and as a tool for environmental good; the exploitation thesis is a critic's.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: It is the opposite pole, the right-wing counterpart to eco-socialism.

collective-farming.rationale: Property-rights and market approaches favour private ownership, including of farmland.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Eco-capitalists defend capitalism and international markets and cooperation.

taxation-theft.rationale: Eco-capitalism depends on state taxes and caps such as carbon taxes, so it rejects the idea that taxation is theft.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Eco-capitalism relies on democratic policy-making, not on exit as the main check.

state-as-business.rationale: The ideology applies market logic to environmental policy, but there is no stated view on running government like a business.

positive-liberty.rationale: Property-rights environmentalism leans on negative liberty; positive liberty is not part of its case.

media-academia-power.rationale: The sources describe policy change through prices and legislation; a claim of media and academic dominance over elected officials is not part of them.

organic-representation.rationale: Eco-capitalism assumes liberal democracy and market institutions, not corporate representation.

total-state.rationale: It seeks to harness markets, limiting direction by the state to setting rules and prices.

national-rebirth.rationale: No decadence or rebirth theme; it is a reformist, pro-market approach.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Market-global ideology; nothing supports territorial expansion.

bound-labor.rationale: Unfree labour is incompatible with markets and the democratic systems that Natural Capitalism calls for.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The approach trusts economics and science-based accounting of natural capital.

single-common-good.rationale: Interest-balancing markets and prices, not a single rationally derived good, are the instrument.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Natural Capitalism calls for democratic governance but keeps conventional firms; mandated votes on running companies are not proposed.

school-vouchers.rationale: Market-friendly adherents may like vouchers but it is outside the environmental literature.

rule-by-example.rationale: It works through rules, prices and law, not moral exemplars.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about tradition, feeling, will or reason in general, not religious faith, which this statement now asks about.

reviewHistory.rationale: The approach is economic and scientific in method, taking its case from cost-benefit and market reasoning.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about tradition, feeling, will or reason in general, not religious faith, which this statement now asks about.

class-collaboration.rationale: Natural Capitalism promises that profit, workers and nature gain together and seeks transitions developed with unions, business and government.

dominated-front.rationale: Eco-capitalism favours integration into world markets and treaties, not blocs against the West.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Nothing in the ideology supports legal gender roles; it speaks of democratic systems.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest and capital markets are part of the capitalism it endorses.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Incompatible with market and democratic principles.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state is a neutral rule-setter fixing market rules, not a class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Eco-capitalism wants fossil costs priced and wind and solar to outcompete fossil fuels.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no basis in or place within the ideology.

national-mission.rationale: No messianic national mission; it favours cooperative international mechanisms.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic policy has no place in a market and rights approach.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Eco-capitalists want the state to set caps, taxes and standards, far beyond a night-watchman role.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Racism has no place in the ideology.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Unstated, but implicit in market-liberal and democratic assumptions.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Socialist doctrine is outside its frame and it is opposed to socialism.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Incompatible with liberal market orientation, though unstated.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Market-based approach, which would not forbid slaughter outright.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Assumed by the democratic, market-based systems Natural Capitalism endorses.

trade-surplus.rationale: Prefers open markets and trading permits to mercantilist surplus-seeking.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Property rights and tort law are central, but eco-capitalists accept state enforcement of caps and taxes.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Eco-capitalism assumes competition among firms for innovation drives environmental progress; it does not extend this to peoples.

separated-powers.rationale: Assumed in the liberal-democratic framework it works within.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Not an eco-capitalist theme; it centres efficiency over distribution.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Nothing in the approach supports it; global-market orientation.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not proposed; it relies on conventional institutions.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Rights- and property-protecting approach, mildly opposed.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price signals are the core mechanism, and price controls distort them.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Nothing in the approach supports it.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Kyoto-style and EU emissions trading rely on pooled authority, but the sources do not take a stance on supranational union.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is unrelated to eco-capitalism's economic and environmental concerns.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Markets in property and housing are accepted.

people-in-arms.rationale: Unrelated to the approach and inconsistent with its pro-state-framework rule.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The approach relies on expertise and economic research.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment is unrelated to eco-capitalism, and adherents split along conservative and liberal lines.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The science-based approach is incompatible with creationism.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debt cancellation is not part of its market framework.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Dependency-theory talk is foreign to it; it sees markets as beneficial.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Eco-capitalism pairs growth with market freedom and democracy; restricting freedom is the eco-authoritarian line.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons policy is unrelated to environmental markets; adherents follow their national security views.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial settlements are unrelated to the ideology.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property rights are central, yet pollution limits qualify them, so adherents hold both sides.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Market economists favour cost-benefit pricing of risks and free-market environmentalists distrust the principle; green capitalists lean the other way.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance obligations are unrelated to the environmental-market focus of the sources.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Natural Capitalism wants to cut income taxes, but no flat-rate proposal.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rule-based markets and property rights require the rule of law.

leader-cult.rationale: Incompatible with its democratic market framework.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court policy is unrelated to eco-capitalism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Secure property rights are central, and redistribution threatens them.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority strategy debates are unrelated to eco-capitalism.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Natural Capitalism treats technological and economic scarcity shifts as drivers of change, but not as a philosophy of history.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Property-rights and tort-law approach relies on courts limiting political majorities.

moral-incentives.rationale: Eco-capitalism's whole premise is that material incentives and profit drive green change.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Revolution is alien to the ideology.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Incompatible with market-global equality of participation.

patriotic-education.rationale: Patriotic schooling is unrelated to the sources, and the market-global orientation gives no direction.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The core claim: capitalism can adapt to environmental crisis by pricing externalities and valuing natural capital.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Post-imperial influence policy is unrelated to the sources.

delink-world-market.rationale: Eco-capitalists want integration into global markets and trading schemes.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Property-rights libertarians may accept it, but mainstream eco-capitalists do not stake out this position.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Property-rights environmentalists favour constitutional protection of property, but eco-capitalism as a whole has no stated view.

elective-rulers.rationale: Assumed by its democratic, market-based framework.

minority-veto.rationale: Nothing supports individual vetoes; pricing schemes need binding collective rules.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Resistance theory is unrelated; the sources assume rule-based democratic governance without discussing remedies.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: A duty of the wealthy is not an eco-capitalist theme, though firms are urged to invest in natural capital.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The ideology is policy-active, aiming to reshape rules and markets.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Critical theory idea outside its frame.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramsci's hegemony appears in critiques of eco-capitalism, not in its own view.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: World-systems and dependency theory reject the market-integration view that eco-capitalists hold.

party-own-road.rationale: Debates among communist parties are unrelated to eco-capitalism.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentism is unrelated to the sources.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A historical dispute unrelated to eco-capitalism.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument controversies are unrelated to the sources.

filial-duty.rationale: Family obligations are unrelated to the sources.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its value turns on whether representatives must follow binding instructions, and the statement now asks only whether voters can recall them at any time.

reviewHistory.rationale: Not part of its institutional picture.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Clearly defined private property is the heart of free-market environmentalism, opposing use-based tenure.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Property-rights markets generally welcome foreign ownership.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Natural Capitalism wants to cut throughput and measure welfare by service quality, but eco-capitalists defend consumer markets.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert foreign policy is unrelated to environmental markets.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Incompatible with its market-democratic, treaty-based framework.

corporate-influence.rationale: Critics claim business opposition to regulation, and the 'Bootleggers and Baptists' theory notes rent-seeking, but eco-capitalism has no stated view on lobbying limits.

job-guarantee.rationale: Natural Capitalism expects more employment from resource productivity, but through markets, not state guarantees.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The law-based market framework assumes obedience to rules and caps.

non-intervention.rationale: International climate cooperation involves obligations to others; mild disagreement.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is unrelated to the environmental-market literature.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy thinking has no place in the ideology.

local-production.rationale: Market-global orientation and trade tools; local self-sufficiency is a green-localist theme, not an eco-capitalist one.

informal-organisation.rationale: Anarchist method alien to the approach.

national-law-over-international.rationale: International regimes such as Kyoto are favoured.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Unrelated to its multilateral market orientation.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Private property is assumed, but the question is posed in a communist frame.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Eco-capitalists hold that capitalism can be both economically beneficial and environmentally protective, though the sources frame it as reformable.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Unrelated and incompatible with market-global orientation.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Eco-capitalism keeps private property and market exchange.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: It is a form of capitalism, so it rejects the call for a third course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Historic claims to land are unrelated to the sources, though secure present property rights are central to the free-market wing.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Denial has no place in the ideology.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Natural Capitalism asks for democratic governance but without prescribing participatory structures.

assisted-dying.rationale: Medical ethics is unrelated to the sources.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Eco-capitalism mixes market and green ideas as a hybrid and is sometimes presented as beyond left and right (Blue Greens).

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Eco-capitalism grounds policy in economics and ecology and in democratic systems, so a divine source of authority conflicts with its secular case.

social-market-economy.rationale: Eco-capitalism wants a market economy with state-set rules, between laissez-faire and statism; social protection is not its focus.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Bloc politics is unrelated to the sources.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Not compatible with its meritocratic market and democratic framework.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Eco-capitalists work through ordinary capital markets and interest.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist claim; eco-capitalism treats nature as capital and does not link the two.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Marxist critique, not shared by adherents.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule-based markets and tort law require standing public rules.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Discrimination has no place in a market-liberal ideology.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religious reform is unrelated to eco-capitalism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Property rights and tort enforcement rely on state justice.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociationalism is unrelated to the sources.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Internal religious governance is unrelated to the sources.

abolish-ip.rationale: Innovation incentives matter to its technology focus.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear weapons basing is unrelated to the sources.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Basing policy is unrelated to the sources.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Historical recognition politics is unrelated to the sources.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Eco-capitalism defends returns to capital, including natural capital and property rights.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Nationalist historiography is unrelated to the sources, and the globally minded orientation inclines against it.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Diaspora politics is unrelated to the sources.

culture-before-state.rationale: National cultural movements are unrelated to the sources.

god-not-male.rationale: Theology is unrelated to the sources.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist theology is unrelated to the sources.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Free-market environmentalists favour private water rights and markets over public control.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Municipalist anarchist form alien to the ideology.

family-wage.rationale: Natural Capitalism mentions living-wage jobs but it is not core.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Eco-capitalism frames nature as capital and policy as economics, with no spiritual dimension in the sources.

dense-cities.rationale: Natural Capitalism covers efficient design but never takes a view on density.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Linguistic nationalism is unrelated to the sources, and a global-market orientation inclines against it.

communal-electorates.rationale: Not compatible with liberal democratic framework.

pollution-taxes.rationale: The central policy: eco-capitalists want externalities priced through a carbon tax or tradable permits so that polluters pay.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Marxist-Leninist revolutionary doctrine contradicts its reformism.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Natural Capitalism calls for fully valuing natural capital, which the eco-capitalism article treats as its premise.

farm-price-support.rationale: Market-based environmentalists oppose subsidies, which they say distort prices and encourage environmental harm.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The free-market wing favours property rights and tort law, but the mainstream strand also accepts carbon taxes and regulation, so adherents are split.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: It holds that markets and prices, not curbs on freedom, solve environmental problems, though it accepts some regulation.

premarital-sex.rationale: Sexual morality is outside the sources; adherents are generally liberal on social matters, an inference.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Outside the sources and adherents hold varied views.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Eco-capitalism accepts more regulation but not planning or public ownership, so it would not defend a nationalised planned economy.

simple-living.rationale: Natural Capitalism aims for abundance through resource productivity and green growth, not for limiting needs or self-sufficiency.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Carbon pricing treats the atmosphere as shared, but property-rights environmentalists favor private ownership; adherents are split.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Carbon taxes raise consumer prices while tax-shifting adherents favor lower other taxes, so views are split.

national-resource-control.rationale: Property-rights advocates favor private ownership while others accept public control; adherents are split.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Natural Capitalism holds that natural capital creates value alongside labour and that markets price it, which contradicts a labour-only theory of value.

missingStatements.text: Pollution should be controlled by a government-set cap on emissions with tradable permits.
missingStatements.rationale: Cap and trade is described as the most popular eco-capitalist idea and was globalised by the Kyoto Protocol.

missingStatements.text: Ecosystems and natural resources should be counted as capital whose value is reflected in the economy.
missingStatements.rationale: Natural Capitalism calls for fully valuing natural capital, which the eco-capitalism article treats as its premise.

missingStatements.text: National economic success should be measured by an indicator that subtracts environmental damage rather than by GDP alone.
missingStatements.rationale: Proponents are reported to favour the Genuine Progress Indicator, which accounts for environmental harm.
missingStatements.declined: Value-1 proposal about the Genuine Progress Indicator; a measurement detail, not a position other ideologies commonly take sides on.

notes: Free-market environmentalists (PERC) distrust regulation and favour property rights and tort law, while Natural Capitalism and carbon-pricing economists accept state-set caps and taxes. Sources do not discuss nuclear power beyond one excerpt that lists it among sources to be phased out, so that answer is split.
